paper.title: The RC6 Block Cipher
paper.venue: AES submission to NIST, version 1.1, August 20, 1998

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: RC6-32/20/b (key schedule with P32/Q32, quadratic function B*(2B+1), data-dependent rotations) written from the paper's pseudocode reproduces all 6 published encryption test vectors of the paper's Appendix: 16-, 24- and 32-byte keys, each with an all-zero and a patterned key/plaintext
Decryption (the paper's inverse procedure) returns the plaintext for all 6

expected_values_source.what: the paper's Appendix 'Test vectors for encryption with RC6' (6 vectors)
expected_values_source.note: vectors extracted from the PDF text by script and compiled in as data; the program was written from the paper's pseudocode

negative_control: built with -DRC6_ROUNDS=19 (one round fewer than the paper's 20), 0 of 6 vectors match and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security analysis and its speed figures (cycles per block)
other word sizes or round counts than RC6-32/20, and key lengths other than 16, 24 and 32 bytes
only six vectors exist in the paper: no larger known-answer set was used
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the six ciphertexts the RC6 paper publishes and inverts them. It does not show the security claims hold.
